title: I Enforced the Maker-Space Soldering-Iron Checkout on the Mentor

parts.text: I checked out iron 4 at 6:18 p.m. and the mentor already had it unlabeled on his bench. The checkout board he built said: TAG OUT. TAG IN. MENTORS INCLUDED. I was twenty-four, night class, holding a board that needed heat now. Mentor Sid said, "Mentors don't tag heat." I pointed at the board. He tinned a tip. "Heat is teaching." I photographed the missing tag, the board, and my checkout slip. Then I asked the tool bot to mark iron 4 overdue on Sid's account. At 6:22 the shop lead asked why Sid's name was on an untagged-iron ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shop lead can see iron 4 on Sid's bench against the tag-out board he built.

social.video_title: The mentor skipped the soldering-iron tag — Part 1/2
social.description: Night class, an unlabeled tip, and a board he built. The bot marked him overdue. Would you have waited on a cold pad?

parts.text: Sid called it a demo until the bot emailed the lead. I printed the ticket, the board, and the photo. I got iron 4. Sid tagged a demo iron and told the benches the board was always about optics. Optics is a word mentors use when a bot exists. Checkout policy now has a second line: HEAT TAGS OUT. I solder. Sid beeps. The tip finally has a name.

social.video_title: Heat tags out like every iron — Part 2/2
social.description: Untagged-iron ticket, a demo with a tag, and a second line on the board. Was teaching ever a missing slip?
